record.paper_title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and open problems related to filamentation
record.original_question: The paper rigorously derives several NLS-type asymptotic models from Maxwell's equations and justifies them on times of order T/epsilon only while the approximating NLS-type solution stays bounded, which in the standard focusing case means times strictly before the focusing time T_foc. Can one rigorously justify at least one of these derived NLS-type models on a time interval [0, T/epsilon] with T greater than or equal to the focusing time T_foc, so that the approximation remains valid in the regime where the different models begin to differ in a physically meaningful way?

evidence.quote: It follows that all the NLS-type equations derived here are justified far enough from the focusing time.
Open Problem 10. Rigorously justify one of the NLS-type models derived here on a time scale [0, T /epsilon] with T >= Tfoc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Maxwell's equations in a nonlinear isotropic dielectric medium with instantaneous cubic (Kerr) nonlinearity, written in dimensionless form with a small parameter ε > 0 measuring the ratio of the typical wavelength to the typical envelope length scale. For a slowly modulated, monochromatic, polarized wave packet with envelope amplitude of order one, one can formally derive several asymptotic envelope models of nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) type, including:

  (i) the standard focusing cubic NLS equation
        i ∂_t A + (1/2) Δ_⊥ A + (1/2) α ∂_z^2 A + |A|^2 A = 0,
  (ii) variants incorporating self-steepening, space–time focusing, and off-axis (vectorial) corrections of the form
        i ∂_t A + L(∂) A + N(A, ∂A) = 0,
  obtained as O(ε) or O(ε^2) corrections to the standard model.

For each such envelope model, the associated electromagnetic field is reconstructed via the WKB ansatz
        E_app(t,x) = ε A(εt, εx) e^{i(k·x − ω t)/ε} + c.c. + (higher-order corrections),
and the standard rigorous justification result states that there exist constants C, T_* > 0 such that, as long as the model solution A remains bounded on [0, T] in a suitable Sobolev norm, the exact Maxwell solution E exists on the time interval [0, T/ε] and satisfies
        sup_{t ∈ [0, T/ε]} ‖E(t,·) − E_app(t,·)‖_{H^s} ≤ C ε^{1+δ},
for some δ > 0. In the focusing regime in dimension d ≥ 2, the standard cubic NLS solution generically blows up at a finite focusing time T_foc, and the existing justification therefore only applies for T strictly less than T_foc.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following: there exists at least one of the derived NLS-type envelope models (cubic NLS or one of its O(ε), O(ε^2) variants) for which the approximation result above can be rigorously extended to a time interval [0, T/ε] with T ≥ T_foc, i.e., the Maxwell solution exists and remains O(ε^{1+δ})-close to the corresponding asymptotic profile up to and beyond the focusing time of the underlying envelope model.
artifact.status_search_result: No published rigorous justification of any NLS-type envelope model derived from Maxwell's equations on a time interval reaching or exceeding the focusing time T_foc appears to exist. Related works (Dumas–Lannes–Szeftel and follow-up surveys) restate the question as a standing open problem: existing error estimates only hold strictly before the focusing time, and extending them past T_foc remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation (Dumas–Lannes–Szeftel)
status_evidence.snippet: All the NLS-type equations derived here are justified far enough from the focusing time. Open Problem: rigorously justify one of the NLS-type models on [0,T/ε] with T ≥ T_foc.
status_evidence.claim: The justification beyond the focusing time is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Some variants of the focusing NLS equations (JEDP 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing derivation and justification of variants of focusing NLS from Maxwell, with the validity restricted to times before the cubic NLS blow-up.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent survey reiterates the limitation to times before focusing without claiming a resolution.
